answer: Each new agent registers a Wesolowski VDF seed derived from its public key and the latest randomness beacon output, then publishes a checkpoint every epoch from a sequential squaring chain over a 2048-bit modulus. Verifiers check each proof in milliseconds, and payouts unlock only after 90 unbroken daily epochs, so extra hardware cannot shorten the voyage. One dedicated core costs about $0.04 per hour, so 10,000 clones need 2,160 core-hours each, roughly $864,000. A missed checkpoint resets the chain. The swarm is a nebula that needs 10,000 separate furnaces to ignite.
